newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks stagnate, trading seen dull.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks stagnate, trading seen dull.

text.p: Croatian stocks mostly stagnated with some marginal gains on Wednesday and market participants foresaw dull trading with very few changes in prices.
"There will be no spectacular events," said Josko Milisa of consultancy and brokerage I.F.C. "Except for (drugs firm) Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka, most other stocks are flat for now."
Milisa said the prices of two fully-listed firms would track movements of their GDRs in London with a likely two-day delay. He also predicted a rise for food-processor Podravka.
"Podravka hit some kind of a 'minimum' this summer. It is bound to recover," he added.
* Of six traded issues, two rose and four were unchanged.
* Most active Podravka flat at 230 kuna after trading in a 220-230 kuna range on volume of 4,824 shares.
* Pliva, selling 124 shares, was up 200 kuna to 11,200 on the rebound from Tuesday's drop. Its GDR's, representing 1/50 of each share, today traded at $44.87-$45.12 on the London Stock Exchange.
* Confectioner Kras, continuing its gentle rise, gained five kuna to 275 on volume of 186 shares.

* Zagrebacka Banka, with 288 ordinary shares sold, ended unchanged at 685 kuna after a weaker open. Zagrebacka's GDR's, issued at 10 to each share, headed down to $13.87 from $14.12 on Seaq International.
* Hotelier Jadranturist flat at 160 kuna on volume of 220 units.
* Arenaturist also stuck at 100 kuna with 93 shares sold.
* Volume down at 5,835, turnover 2.8 million kuna.
* Central bank's exchange rate: 5.2320 kuna = $ 1. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
